title: A smooth algebra over a normal ring is a normal ring
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings which is smooth in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] ($S$ finitely presented over $R$, $H_1(L_{S/R})=0$, $\Omega_{S/R}$ finite projective). If $R$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] (every localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ at a prime is a normal domain), then $S$ is a normal ring.

proof.text: Prove the Noetherian case in the private lemma smooth_normal_noetherian. Finite type makes the target Noetherian; smoothness supplies flatness. Each fibre is smooth over its residue field, which is regular, hence the fibre is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] and normal by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-normal-fibres-noetherian-normal].

proof.text: For a smooth map from an integrally closed domain, obtain the filtered diagram and its ring equivalence from [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-normal-domain-approximation]. Apply the preceding Noetherian case to each displayed smooth model map, then [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-normal-ring] to the diagram. Transport the normality of prime localizations across Localization.localRingEquiv, using Function.Injective.isDomain and IsIntegrallyClosed.of_equiv. This is the private lemma smooth_normal_domain.

proof.text: For a prime $q$ of $S$, put $p=f^{-1}(q)$, $A=R_p$ and $B=A\otimes_R S$. The hypotheses supply IsDomain A and IsIntegrallyClosed A. Smooth base change and smooth_normal_domain give normality of B. With its right-factor S-algebra structure, B is the localization of S at the image M of the complement of p, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change]. M is disjoint from q, as shown elementwise in the proof. IsLocalization.isPrime_of_isPrime_disjoint makes qB prime, and under_map_of_isPrime_disjoint computes its contraction as q. The theorem isLocalization_isLocalization_atPrime_isLocalization identifies B localized at qB as an S-localization at q. IsLocalization.algEquiv then gives an equivalence to S_q, and normality transports by Function.Injective.isDomain and IsIntegrallyClosed.of_equiv.
